title: Making a banner for the bannerless

words.meaning: for the one without a banner, for what has no sign
words.context: Bhāskara: «असत्यस्मिन्नज्ञापकाय», for what has no mark to make it known

words.role: with ajāyathāḥ: ‘you were born together with’

sandhi.rule: m before k becomes the class nasal ṅ; a final n after a short vowel is doubled before a vowel (P. 8.3.32 (ङमो ह्रस्वादचि ङमुण्नित्यम्))
-aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o; -āḥ before a vowel loses its visarga
m joins the following vowel; -iḥ before a vowel becomes -ir

morphology.note: instrumental plural of uṣas, ‘dawn’, with the stem uṣad- before a consonant ending; Bhāskara cites the rule for the t: «दृक् स्ववस्स्वतवसाम्».
negative compound a- + ketu, ‘that which has no banner’.

translation.literal: Making a banner for the bannerless, form for the formless, O men, you were born together with the dawns.
translation.readable: You give a sign to what has none and form to what is formless, O men: you were born with the dawns.

meaning: A verse of light at daybreak: one born with the dawns gives a sign to what has none and form to what is formless. The address ‘O men’ (maryāḥ) and the second person make it a riddle in the Ṛgveda (1.6.3). Its first word is ketu, ‘banner’, which is also the name of the graha Ketu, and in the Navagraha sūktam it is Ketu’s own mantra. The choice belongs to the later gṛhya tradition, which does not state its reason; none is added here.
in_the_rite: Step 9 (Ketu), first mantra. The use of a Vedic verse for a graha belongs to the later gṛhya tradition; the commentary below speaks of the verse in its Vedic setting. In the Saṃhitā (TS 7.4.20.1) it belongs to the attendance on the horse of the Aśvamedha; Bhāskara says a banner is fastened on with it.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Bhaṭṭa Bhāskara: with this verse a banner is fastened, «ध्वजं प्रतिमुञ्चति - केतुं ध्वजं कृण्वन् कुर्वन्तु»; the ‘form’ is «पेशः रूपं रूपवृन्दं हे मर्याः मनुष्याः», and the last line he takes as ‘be born as if with blazing flames’, «उषद्भिः ज्वलद्भिरिव समजायथाः».

notes.label: linguistic
notes.text: A gāyatrī of three eight-syllable pādas. The Taittirīya and the Ṛgveda (1.6.3) have the same words.
